newsitem.title: USA: Potential Brent onslaught punishes U.S. cash crude.
newsitem.headline: Potential Brent onslaught punishes U.S. cash crude.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices declined Thursday on technical pressure in paper markets, while domestic grade barrels were squeezed by potential new flows of foreign crudes to the Gulf.
Cash dealers said market fundamentals took a slightly more bearish tint on the widening Brent-West Texas Intermediate/Cushing spread, a likely foreshadowing of North Sea Brent offerings.

Favorable arbitrage numbers left June Brent with a more than $1.85 discount to corresponding WTI/Cushing. In addition to bearish sentiment from the new arb opening, prices were pushed lower by a heavier than expected June Brent program.
Traders thought a number of planned maintenance programs in the North Sea would deflate volumes for June. The levels were lower, but not as thin as forecast, traders said.
The June Brent loading program will consist of 38.4 cargoes, down from 41.8 cargoes in May.
In the Gulf, two trade houses were offering Brent for delivery June 22-28 and June 25-July 2, asking around WTI/Cushing minus 70-80 cents a barrel.
On the domestic grade front, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James fell back around five cents to trade between flat to five cents over benchmark WTI/Cushing.
Midland/WTI sold at 35-37 cents under WTI, down four cents from late Wednesday.
Other trades had West Texas Sour/Midland flat at around $1.45-40 under the marker, and Eugene Island at WTI/Cushing -$1.55, traders said.

June exchange for physicals (EFP's) were talked at plus five to seven cents, pulling back from earlier in the week. Traders said the retreat was due to most players already filling their needs, and not reflective of a change in market psychology.
June EFP's have gained on expectations foreign Bonny Light from Nigeria will be delivered against June NYMEX contracts.
